description.text: YUM has over 63,000 restaurants in 155 countries and territories primarily operating under the four concepts of KFC, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and Habit Burger & Grill (the “Concepts”). The Company’s KFC, Taco Bell and Pizza Hut brands are global leaders of the chicken, Mexican-inspired food and pizza categories, respectively. Habit Burger & Grill is a fast-casual restaurant concept specializing in made-to-order chargrilled burgers, sandwiches and more. At December 31, 2025, 97% of our Concepts’ units are operated by independent franchisees or licensees under the terms of franchise or license agreements. The terms franchise or franchisee within this Form 10-K are meant to describe third parties that operate units under either franchise or license agreements. In 2025, we began a review of strategic options for the Pizza Hut brand. The objective of the review is to create value for YUM, Pizza Hut and its franchise partners by determining the optimal approach to best capitalize on Pizza Hut's structural advantages — strong brand equity, experienced franchise partners and meaningful scale — in the highly fragmented pizza market. We currently intend to complete this strategic options review in 2026, and there can be no assurance this review will result in any specific outcome or transaction. Brands, Inc., and its subsidiaries franchise or operate more than 44,000 restaurants in 151 countries and territories under its iconic brands - KFC, Taco Bell and Habit Burger & Grill. KFC and Taco Bell are global leaders in the chicken and Mexican-inspired food categories, respectively. Habit is a fast-casual concept known for fresh, cooked-to-order food. Fueled by Yum!'s Recipe for Good Growth and its Raising the B.A.R priorities, Yum! combines the strength of its global brands, franchise system, scale and leading digital and technology capabilities to drive growth, create long-term value, and build the world's most loved, trusted and connected restaurant brands.

analysis_md:
# YUM — Yum! Brands, Inc.
v5 run, 2026-10-14 (supersedes the v4 run of 2026-10-13; same conclusion, rebuilt under the v5 data gate with the base pinned from ttm.json via `--ttm`). Scope note: engine market cap is $41.324B at $147.06 (nasdaq_quote_api) — it has drifted just over the $40B line since the universe was built; `in_scope_under_40b` is recorded as false on current numbers, noted, not re-scoped.

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, or key_numbers.md — none are recomputed. Balance-sheet debt context beyond the engine's output is from cited web search results and is flagged where the engine's own figure is wrong.

## What it is
The world's largest restaurant franchisor: KFC, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut, and the small Habit Burger Grill, overwhelmingly franchisee-owned and operated (search results put the system at 63,778 restaurants at Q2 2026, up 5% year over year). YUM mostly collects royalties, franchise fees, and rent on franchisee sales — an asset-light royalty toll on other people's capex, plus a minority of company-owned stores. Q2 2026 prints (search results): revenue $2.17B, up 12.2% year over year; worldwide same-store sales +3% (Taco Bell +7%, KFC +2%); worldwide system sales +5% excluding foreign currency; excluding Pizza Hut, system sales +7% ex-FX, unit count +6%, core operating profit +8%, and digital was more than 60% of system sales; adjusted EPS $1.62, up 12.5%.

## Owner's earnings
History (SEC EDGAR 10-Ks, conservative = OCF − capex − SBC, from financials_history.csv): OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Conservative OE totals: $1,401M (2021), $1,064M (2022), $1,223M (2023), $1,363M (2024), $1,569M (2025). Latest-FY OE/share is $5.58 (dcf_numbers.json).
- FY2025 conservative OE: OCF $2,010,000,000 − capex $371,000,000 − SBC $70,000,000 = $1,569,000,000 (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_total_latest_fy). SBC is small here and charged in full.
- Maintenance version FY2025 (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC, from financials_history.csv): $1,719,000,000 — above the conservative figure, which supports OE quality; the conservative number stays the base for screen consistency.
- **Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, saved to ttm.json, applied via `--ttm`; base_source: ttm_json):**
  - OCF: FY $2,010,000,000 − prior YTD $850,000,000 + current YTD $923,000,000 = **TTM $2,083,000,000**
  - Capex: FY $371,000,000 − prior YTD $142,000,000 + current YTD $175,000,000 = **TTM $404,000,000**
  - SBC: FY $70,000,000 − prior YTD $37,000,000 + current YTD $35,000,000 = **TTM $68,000,000**
  - Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **278,000,000**
  - **TTM OE total $1,611,000,000 → base OE/share $5.79** (dcf_numbers.json base_oe_per_share $5.794964028776978)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $4.78/share — not used as the base: it is anchored on the 2022–23 trough years and is 9.4 months stale. The TTM base *raises* value versus the median and the verdict still fails by a wide margin (see method range), so the choice is not load-bearing.
- Q2 2026 GAAP earnings are distorted by Pizza Hut sale-related tax items (per the prior filing review retained in this folder's v4 analysis: a large non-cash deferred tax benefit triggered by signing the sale). The OCF-based conservative OE is clean of those items because the cash-flow statement backs deferred taxes out before OCF — this is why the OE series, not GAAP net income, is the base.

## Moat: 7/10 — strong franchisor moat
Justification: Two global category leaders (KFC, Taco Bell) run as a ~97%-franchised royalty toll with proven pricing power and returns on capital held through cycles — against zero consumer switching costs, demonstrated brand decay inside this same portfolio (Pizza Hut), franchisee-health dependence, and high leverage that limits downturn flexibility.
- FOR: KFC and Taco Bell are the default global brands in chicken and Mexican-inspired QSR — brand mindshare built over decades is what franchisees pay royalties for; the franchise toll model itself (growth funded by franchisee capex while YUM clips high-margin royalties, OE positive 5/5 years including through COVID and the 2022 margin squeeze); scale in purchasing, advertising funds, and development across ~64k units no regional rival matches; the Byte by Yum! tech platform and >60% digital mix ex-Pizza Hut, raising franchisee switching friction; proven pricing power — repeated menu price takes with system sales still compounding ~5% ex-FX.
- AGAINST: End consumers have zero switching costs — the moat runs through franchisees and habit, not lock-in, and QSR is in an open value war; brand decay is demonstrably possible inside this portfolio — Pizza Hut shrank to negative comps and is being sold (below); franchisee health is the real balance sheet (a single master-franchisee termination can close hundreds of units at once); secular/regulatory pressure — GLP-1 appetite suppression, labor and commodity inflation, food-safety headline risk; high leverage (see FLAGS) limits buyback support in a downturn.
- A 7 gives CAP = 11.1 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 11.1 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-14)
Growth recalibration (written reason, per the standing rule): the engine's blended growth is 9.33% (g_blend 8.29% plus a +1.05pp buyback adjustment), but two blend components are artifacts — the 14.06% OE/share CAGR (2y) is measured off the 2022 trough, and latest revenue YoY is +8.81%. The prints that mean something: system sales +5% ex-FX in Q2 2026 (+7% ex-Pizza Hut), core operating profit +8% ex-Pizza Hut, adjusted EPS +12.5% (flattered by tax items). Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.1233 / −0.0633 / −0.0183 / +0.0167 / +0.0567 vs g_base) to −3.0% / +3.0% / **+7.5%** / +11.0% / +15.0%. Sanity check: base +7.5% sits on the ex-Pizza Hut core profit print and below the adjusted-EPS print — defensible. Bull +11.0% is roughly the adjusted-EPS growth rate sustained. Super bull +15.0% is above every current print — written reason: it requires the announced buyback funded by Pizza Hut sale proceeds compounding per-share OE on top of mid-single-digit system growth plus a clean exit; that is a stretch case and carries only 10% weight. Probabilities are the defaults 10/25/30/25/10 — a mostly-franchised royalty stream is steadier than most of this universe, and the leverage / Pizza Hut transition risks are carried in the growth starts and bear multipliers rather than a probability skew. OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $147.06.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -3.0% | 0.75 | Value war + franchisee stress + leverage bite | $27.54 | 4.62% |
| Bear | 25% | 3.0% | 0.90 | Low-single-digit system growth, margin pressure | $43.79 | 6.25% |
| Base | 30% | 7.5% | 1.00 | KFC/Taco Bell compound, Pizza Hut exit roughly per-share neutral | $60.20 | 7.88% |
| Bull | 25% | 11.0% | 1.10 | Adjusted-EPS-rate growth sustained, buyback compounds | $78.20 | 9.55% |
| Super bull | 10% | 15.0% | 1.25 | Full buyback + clean exit + sustained double-digit per-share growth | $107.48 | 12.04% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $62.06, IV@12% $83.48, IV@10% $107.54, weighted IRR 8.08%, base-case IRR 7.88%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 3.94%, terminal value 20.10% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.90x, 9.43 months since FY end. The low terminal-value share matters: the D is not a terminal-value artifact — the near-term cash flows themselves are too small for the price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 9.43 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, quoted above and applied via `--ttm` (base_source: ttm_json). This is the only flag on the final run.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (fired on the preliminary run at 4.47x): the final recalibrated run's spread is 3.90x and the flag no longer fires, but 3.90x is still wide in absolute terms — it reflects a genuine fork (levered franchisor compounding vs value-war/GLP-1 erosion), so confidence is held at medium regardless.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT — manual flag, the engine MISSED this and its printed net-debt figure is wrong:** dcf_numbers.json reports net debt of −$671,000,000 (net cash) because EDGAR's LongTermDebtNoncurrent series comes back empty for YUM (debt_lt is blank in financials_history.csv). Search results on the actual filings say the opposite: total borrowings were about $12.28B at June 30, 2026 (short-term borrowings $2.81B), up from about $11.91B at the end of 2025. OE here is measured after cash interest (OCF-based), so the DCF is not double-counting the debt — the leverage instead caps buyback flexibility in a downturn and is a core reason the bear book carries real weight. It does not change the tier, which is set by the weighted IRR, but no reader should trust the engine's net-debt diagnostic for this name.
- **BASIS_BREAK — forward, manual (the engine's historical test cannot see a signed-but-unclosed sale):** search results report YUM agreed in June 2026 to sell Pizza Hut to LongRange Capital for $2.7B, with closing expected in Q3 2026, proceeds earmarked for revolver repayment and buybacks, and transition services phasing out during 2027. The TTM base therefore still contains Pizza Hut — the weakest brand (negative U.S. comps in 2025, per search results) — while the forward company will not. The per-share math roughly self-corrects (losing Pizza Hut's OE while retiring share count with the proceeds), which is why scenario starts are set on KFC/Taco Bell-led prints rather than consolidated prints that straddle the break. Any Q3 2026 gain on sale will inflate GAAP earnings, not OE.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE — 2026, manual (post-FY, so the engine's FY test did not fire):** resolved in the Owner's earnings section — Pizza Hut sale-related deferred tax benefits sit in GAAP net income, are backed out of OCF, and never touch the base. Adjusted EPS ($1.62 in Q2, +12.5%) is the honest earnings print.
- Red flags checked, none found that change the run: dilution — none (TTM SBC $68,000,000 on TTM OCF of $2,083,000,000; diluted count fell from 282,000,000 prior-YTD to 278,000,000 current-YTD per ttm.json); customer concentration — none (a ~64k-unit franchise system); going concern — none. Food-safety/brand headlines and GLP-1 exposure are carried in the moat AGAINST section, not as separate flags.

## My thoughts / overlay
- **Method range is narrow and entirely in D.** The preliminary run (3-yr-median base $4.78, engine-default growth and probabilities) gave weighted IRR 7.54% and IV@15% $55.67; the final run (TTM base, recalibrated growth, moat 7) gives 8.08% and $62.06. Every defensible input set lands in Tier D. Even the super-bull scenario (15% growth start, OE ×1.25, 10% weight) only reaches a 12.04% IRR / $107.48 IV@15% — below today's price at a 15% discount rate. There is no honest version of this model where $147.06 clears 15%.
- The business quality is not the debate — a 7/10-moat franchisor with 5/5 positive OE years and a self-funding buyback is a genuinely good asset. The debate is purely price: at $147.06 against TTM OE/share of $5.79, the OE yield is 3.94%, and the market is paying today for a decade of clean compounding from a levered balance sheet with a brand sale mid-flight.
- The Pizza Hut exit is strategically right (removes the decaying brand, funds debt repayment and buybacks) and roughly per-share neutral — a quality improvement, not a valuation rescue. Watch: closing terms in Q3 2026 results, pace of buybacks, Taco Bell comp durability against the value war, and any food-safety escalation.
- **Hurdle math (from key_numbers.md / dcf_numbers.json, not recomputed):** the stock clears Andrew's 15% hurdle only at the weighted IV@15% of $62.06 — the weighted IV sits 57.80% below the price (upside_at_15 is −57.80%). A buyer wanting a margin of safety below the weighted IV needs a materially lower price still. This is a watchlist-at-a-very-different-price name, not a near-miss.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (tier by numbers D — no override; weighted IRR 8.08%, and no scenario at any defensible weight clears 15% at $147.06)
- Confidence: **Medium** (filing-derived TTM base and a narrow D-across-methods range, held back from high by the 3.90x scenario spread, the real leverage the engine failed to see, and the mid-flight Pizza Hut divestiture)
- One-liner: see judgment.json / score.json.
